audience: homeowners and renters setting up a smart home
reviewedBy: Claude via the v8/v9/v10 three-way diff, presented to Tyler 2026-09-16; not independently reviewed by Tyler

base.rationale: Buyers compare specs, app reviews and ecosystem compatibility before each device purchase, and the household's main worry is whether it will actually work reliably with what they already own.

scenarios.label: DIY security bundle
scenarios.description: A household choosing a video doorbell plus matching indoor/outdoor cameras and a storage plan to cover entrances and key rooms.

scenarios.label: Whole-home lighting plan
scenarios.description: Planning bulbs, switches, and strips room-by-room while balancing renter-safe options versus wired installs and scene control.

scenarios.label: Robot vacuum choice
scenarios.description: Selecting a robot vacuum/mop that reliably handles the home's floor types, pet hair, mapping, and app ecosystem integration.

scenarios.label: Standardized expansion buy
scenarios.description: After standardizing on a brand, one person quickly orders more of the same bulbs/plugs/sensors to finish additional rooms.

cellTexts: [problem_recognition|DIY security bundle|generic] i'm away a lot. porch pirates hit our block and someone tried the back gate last week. i need a way to know when someone's on my property and to scare them off, but i rent so drilling is tricky.

[problem_recognition|Whole-home lighting plan|generic] our lights are all over the place - some rooms blazing, others dim, and we keep forgetting switches. i'd love the house to shift brighter in the day and warmer at night without me babysitting it, and guests shouldn't be confused.

[problem_recognition|Robot vacuum choice|generic] two shedding dogs + toddler crumbs + hardwood and rugs. i can't keep up. need something that keeps floors under control on its own and doesn't choke on cords or shoelaces.

[problem_recognition|Standardized expansion buy|generic] finished an attic space. i want add-ons that talk to what i already use, battery powered, tiny, stick-on if possible, and absolutely no extra hub. just need the upstairs to join the same routines.
[category_education|-|generic] dumb question: what does a smart home setup actually do, in plain english? what are the main pieces and how do they talk to each other?

[discovery|DIY security bundle|generic] what's the best diy home security kit for a small house with a front porch? needs phone alerts, an outdoor camera option, loud siren, and renter-friendly install.

[discovery|Whole-home lighting plan|generic] best smart lighting route for a whole house without rewiring? mix of switches and bulbs is fine. want dimming, color temp that shifts by time of day, and simple wall control for guests.
[discovery|Robot vacuum choice|generic] best robot vacuum for hardwood plus low-pile rugs, heavy pet hair, good mapping, avoids cords, and ideally a self-empty base?
[discovery|Standardized expansion buy|generic] best add-on smart home sensors for expanding an existing setup without adding a new hub? need battery power, quick pairing, small size, and solid range.
[shortlist|DIY security bundle|generic] can you narrow it to 3 strong diy home security kits for a small place with a porch, loud siren, and no-drill install?
[shortlist|Whole-home lighting plan|generic] give me 3 smart lighting approaches to cover a whole house - bulbs vs switch replacements vs a mix - that won't confuse guests.
[shortlist|Robot vacuum choice|generic] please shortlist 3 robot vacuums that handle pet hair, avoid cords, map well, and can empty themselves.
[shortlist|Standardized expansion buy|generic] shortlist 3-4 battery-powered, stick-on sensors that pair fast with an existing system and don't need a new hub. reliable range, low false alarms.

[criteria|DIY security bundle|generic] Trying to piece together my own home security kit for a small two story house. What actually matters when comparing options? Beyond camera resolution, like sensor range, local storage, battery backup, cellular failover, false alarm handling, monitoring fees - what should be on the checklist?

[criteria|Whole-home lighting plan|generic] Designing a whole-home smart lighting plan for a 3 bedroom place. What should I prioritize so it scales and doesn't annoy guests? Bulbs vs switches, dimming on 3-way circuits, color accuracy, Matter or hub, scene controllers, wall plate feel, power limits - what actually matters?

[criteria|Robot vacuum choice|generic] First robot vac. What specs really predict good cleaning and fewer headaches? Navigation type, obstacle avoidance, suction vs airflow, brush design for long hair, noise, mapping and no-go zones, bin size, self-empty, maintenance costs - what should I focus on?

[criteria|Standardized expansion buy|generic] I'm standardizing the house on one line of sensors and switches so future add-ons are painless. What specs should I lock down now to avoid surprises later - protocol, radio range, load ratings, 3-way support, firmware update path, device IDs/labels, warranty, replacement availability?

[feature_screening|DIY security bundle|generic] Which DIY security setups include all of these: a battery-backed base station, local video storage accessible without a subscription, cellular backup for internet outages, and door/window sensors with at least 5 year battery life?

[feature_screening|Whole-home lighting plan|generic] I need lighting that does automatic circadian color temperature and works on 3-way circuits where there's no neutral at the switch. Which options check both boxes?
[feature_screening|Robot vacuum choice|generic] Which robot vacuums can reliably avoid cords and pet waste, have a self-empty dock plus auto-wash for the mop pad, and support per-room no-go zones?

[feature_screening|Standardized expansion buy|generic] Looking for contact sensors that are Zigbee 3.0, use CR2032 batteries, report temperature, include a tamper switch, and support OTA firmware updates through a standard hub. What models meet that spec?

[use_case|DIY security bundle|generic] I want alerts if the back gate opens after 10 pm, an indoor siren, and outdoor cameras that still record if the internet drops. Detached garage has spotty Wi-Fi and we get winter power outages. What would you put together to cover that?

[use_case|Whole-home lighting plan|generic] Goal: whole-home lighting that feels normal for guests but gives me scenes. Wall switches must work even if the app is down, motion in hall and pantry, warm dim at night, bright cool in the kitchen for meal prep, and a vacation mode that looks lived in. How would you lay this out room by room?

[use_case|Robot vacuum choice|generic] Two shedding dogs, mostly hardwood, one rug with fringe, lots of chair legs and cables. I want a robot vac that runs while we're out, avoids cords and water bowls, respects virtual barriers at stairs, and won't choke on dark floors. What setup and features should I go for?

[use_case|Standardized expansion buy|generic] Rolling out a dozen more smart dimmers to match what's already installed. I want identical behavior on 3-way circuits, same paddles and status LEDs, and one template for firmware and min/max trim I can clone room to room. What's the cleanest workflow to stage, label, and deploy without breaking existing automations?

[social_validation|-|generic] What are homeowners actually happy with for smart home gear this year? Looking for stuff people keep after a year, not launch hype. Any products that get consistently strong long-term reviews and have active community support or good how-to guides?

[comparison|DIY security bundle|Amazon] Trying to pick a DIY security bundle: Google Nest or Amazon? Small house, want doorbell cam, 2 outdoor cams, a keypad, and good app alerts. Which one actually works smoother day to day?

[comparison|Whole-home lighting plan|Apple] Whole-home lighting setup: if I'm already on iPhone, should I lean Apple or Google Nest for controlling scenes, schedules, and motion automations across like 40 bulbs and 6 switches?

[comparison|Robot vacuum choice|Philips Hue] Choosing a robot vac that plays nice with the rest of the house: building around Google Nest vs Philips Hue, which ecosystem makes it easier to start, stop, and tie cleaning into routines?

[comparison|DIY security bundle|Ecobee] For a DIY security kit, Google Nest vs Ecobee: sensors, indoor cam, doorbell, and self-monitoring now with option to add pro later. Which is less finicky and more reliable?

[premium_worth|-|generic] Expanding a setup room by room. For smart plugs, motion sensors, contact sensors: is the premium brand actually worth it over the store brand if I care about uptime, firmware support, and Matter compatibility? Or is the cheap stuff good enough if specs match?
[objections|DIY security bundle|generic] Honest take: does Google Nest lag on motion alerts or miss events? I don't want a break-in and the clip shows up 2 minutes late. Wifi isn't perfect here.

[objections|Whole-home lighting plan|generic] Planning whole-home lighting and worried Google Nest routines will be slow or out of sync. Do lights end up stuttering or missing triggers when you scale to a few dozen devices?
[objections|Robot vacuum choice|generic] If I control the robot vac through Google Nest, is voice and routine reliability solid, or do commands time out and the bot just sits there?

[objections|Standardized expansion buy|generic] Rolling out 50 plus devices over the next few months. Any performance ceilings with Google Nest I should expect? Device cap, routine latency, Thread/Matter stability at that scale?

[pricing|DIY security bundle|generic] What is the real all-in cost for a Google Nest DIY security setup for a small house? Hardware for 1 doorbell, 3 cams, sensors, plus Nest Aware after the free trial. Is pro monitoring required or can I skip the monthly?

[pricing|Whole-home lighting plan|generic] Budgeting a whole-home lighting plan: per-room, is it cheaper long term to do smart switches and dumb bulbs, or smart bulbs everywhere? Any hidden costs like bridges or subscription fees I should factor in?

[pricing|Robot vacuum choice|generic] Robot vac pricing: is paying extra for lidar mapping and auto-empty worth it if it's a 2-bed apartment with mixed floors and a dog? Or will a midrange model do basically the same job?

[pricing|Standardized expansion buy|generic] Standardizing on Google Nest. Adding 6 more cameras and a bunch of sensors this year. Cheapest way to cover storage and alerts: does one Nest Aware subscription cover all cams, and what does that do to per-camera cost after year one?

[churn_triggers|-|generic] I've been on Google Nest for years (thermostat + cams). Is it still the right ecosystem to stick with, or is it time to rethink? What does Nest still do best that I'd miss if I switch?
[alternatives|-|defensive] If I don't go with Google Nest for a small house (renter), what are the best alternatives for a doorbell, thermostat, and two or three cameras that work well together?
[alternatives|-|Amazon] Not loving Amazon for smart home anymore. What are the best alternatives for voice control, lights, plugs, a doorbell cam, and simple routines in a one-bedroom rental?

[alternatives|-|Apple] Don't want to lock into Apple for smart home. What are the best non-Apple options that cover lights, cameras, thermostat, plus a video doorbell and a smart lock without a lot of hub hassle?
[alternatives|-|Philips Hue] Hue feels pricey. What are good alternatives for full-color smart bulbs and light strips that still do scenes and reliable schedules?
[alternatives|-|Ecobee] What are solid alternatives to Ecobee for a smart thermostat that handles multi-stage heat/cool and has good occupancy detection? System is heat pump + gas furnace.

[problem_resolution|-|generic] my google nest thermostat keeps running the fan in the middle of the night even with the schedule off. how do i stop that? could eco mode, auto-schedule, or safety temps be forcing it?

[expansion|-|generic] I've got Google Nest running great at home (thermostat, doorbell). Thinking of rolling it out to our rental cabin too. How do I set it up so guests and cleaners can use what they need without giving them my account?

[ecosystem|-|generic] What plays nicely with Google Nest right now? Looking for smart switches, locks, shades, garage opener, and contact/motion sensors that integrate cleanly with Google Home and Matter.

[advocacy|-|generic] Friend thinks smart home is a headache. If I want to recommend Google Nest, what's the straight-shooting case to make? They care about privacy, easy setup, and not babysitting automations.
